# Independent audit: quantitative face exhaustion and the linear buffer gap

Source read in full:
`candidate 5dc06bb8226350eb`,
Sections 1--8. Verdict: PASS. No substantive repair is required.

The single-input enlargement is actual: every resulting fiber lies between
K_z and K_z+tB, and its input fiber is exactly K_u+tB. The displayed upper
and lower mass estimates follow from the two homothetic inclusions; the
depth estimate uses old-body section bounds after the measure comparison,
so it is uniform in unbounded base tilts and includes supporting caps.
Every face not containing u is unchanged, and exact face isolation keeps
all depths on those faces unchanged, not merely their own volumes.

If the near-deepest faces miss u, t=eta/(2C_D) keeps raw Q exactly fixed
while increasing mass. The lower improvement in (7) and the contradiction
g>=2g with eta=2g/c_F are correct. The expansion competes with the full
ordinary infimum, not just the compact representative class. The g=0 case
is separately supplied by exact face exhaustion.

The distance-to-boundary Lipschitz estimate puts each chosen near-deepest
mark in the stated uniform own ball. For any base in its minimal face,
the fixed positive anchored coefficient and own-ball segment give the
parameter domination (12). This works for arbitrary nonnegative concave
parameters; it is not an affine-parameter argument. Log normalization
then supplies a marked value at least c_L.

The own-ball strip estimate, together with the separate pure-base gap,
proves (15) for every cap. It does not require cap attainment, stationarity,
or smallness of the ACTUAL marked multiplier. The displayed epsilon
restriction makes the fixed lower strip and pure-base budgets compatible.

For changing bodies, the two bounds are precisely

    beta_epsilon-beta_* >= g,
    beta_epsilon-beta_* >= c_B epsilon-(H-1)g.

Their maximum is at least c_B epsilon/H for every g>=0. Thus the proof
does not assume an unknown convergence rate of bodies relative to epsilon.
The large-g and outside-bad-sublevel cases are separated correctly. The
upper bound uses the already attained ordinary minimum or uniform ordinary
near-minimizers with L=1. The compact positive/minor-quota framework remains
an explicit dependency.

Section 8 is also correct. A tilted row with source p is supported over
its minimal base face. Its touching affine plane is nonnegative on that
face's actual hull, so the same finite anchored coefficient and source ball
bound A_i/L_i by C_0 there. The original row is a probability, and hence

    0<=KL(bar_rho_i || rho_i)<=log C_0.

This is only a one-sided likelihood comparison; the source correctly makes
no original-row mean or reverse-density assertion.

The theorem proves a two-sided value gap and a row comparison. It does not
by itself prove optimized-value differentiability, a joint scalar/body
separator, or Gamma cap payment. Those scopes are preserved.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
